transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just done your post-cataract surgery follow-up check with you. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is considered light exercise, which means you can start doing it after 1 week from your surgery.

Just make sure to be careful about getting water in your eye while you're gardening, especially in the first month after surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful to know. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific instructions for your gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or the bottle itself for how to use it.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thanks for that. Another thing I wanted to ask is, I've been feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. 

Are you experiencing mild sensitivity, or is it more severe with pain and redness?
transcript.delivered: Yes, some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That would help me give you better advice about what to expect right now.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Okay, so at about a week post-surgery, some blurriness is still normal and should improve over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay. So keep an eye on how it's progressing.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have been. Thank you again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! I'm glad I could help. Take care and best of luck with your recovery.
